calculations.description: Frozen CAD/NOK reference 6.6046853997; five-year percentile about 0.0397 and z-score -2.15. These are historical screen statistics, not a post-event mark or a valuation target. No position sizing or expected-return estimate has been validated.

claim: November 4 opportunity review saved at the actual write time. Screen long CAD/NOK as an independent conditional trade, not an executed position or a required hedge for CORRA. The frozen cross was 6.6046854, near its five-year bottom (about 4th percentile, z-score -2.15). That identifies an extreme, not fair value. If energy-risk premia fade and exceptional NOK strength unwinds more than CAD strength, the cross could rise. The authorized election article's reported oil fall motivates checking this channel; it does not establish a post-election CAD/NOK entry or a durable change in the energy regime. Before proposing an entry, require the next common post-event FX observation and a coherent decomposition of relative oil sensitivity, domestic policy/growth, broad USD/risk beta and financing. CAD and NOK are both energy currencies; the sign is empirical and may differ by regime. Shared oil/disinflation exposure with CORRA is a portfolio sizing question. No arbitrary single-FX cap, mandatory hedge relationship, or negative-correlation veto applies. Kevin's AUDNZD example informs the method, not the choice of this trade.

competing_explanations.statement: The five-year extreme may reflect a structural relative-rate, fiscal or external-balance change rather than a temporary energy premium.
CAD may weaken more than NOK when oil falls; a shared producer label does not establish relative beta.
Broad risk-on can support both currencies with changing relative effects. A stable historical correlation is not assumed.

evidence.note: Original shared November 4 freeze; underlying observations have their own dates. CORRA 2027 H/M/U/Z 2.970/3.115/3.225/3.310, fixing 2.54; Canada underlying 1.85, unemployment 6.5. Composite packet's later prices are not substituted into this morning assessment.

Explicitly authorized by Kevin after the freeze. Article reports Democratic House/Senate majorities, lower Treasury yields and roughly 8% lower oil. Reported quotations are asynchronous context, not executable marks. Receipt minute in conversation was not recorded. Fiscal constraint and Iran de-escalation are hypotheses, not established consequences.

ACP 389: reject CLOSE/flat recommendation. It excluded authorized election context from reasoning, imposed unsupported one-FX/risk caps, used missing NZ bond data as a blanket spot ban, and substituted arbitrary stress asymmetry for expected-value evidence. Verifier approval did not catch all sign errors.

Kevin's component-risk lesson already saved as edge revision 02. Opposite directional responses need not form a hedge; correlated positions are not automatically duplicates. AUDNZD discussion was an illustration, not an instruction to sell.

falsifiers.statement: NOK outperformance persists during sustained oil declines, contradicting the assumed relative energy transmission.
Relative policy or growth repricing favors NOK enough to offset any energy-premium reversal.
The next common packet shows the cross already repriced sufficiently that the residual expected reward no longer compensates the downside and financing.

forecast.expectation: Conditional prospective forecast: if subsequent shared evidence confirms fading energy premia and greater reversal of NOK's exceptional strength than CAD's, expect CAD/NOK appreciation over the following two to six weeks. Until that condition and a common reference price are available, this remains a candidate with no position, target or executable entry.
forecast.horizon: 2–6 weeks after evidence confirms the stated condition; review next shared session
forecast.metric: CAD/NOK spot and relative energy, policy/growth and risk components

title: Conditional long CAD/NOK: test relative energy-premium reversal
